logline: Three teenagers discover inherited superpowers while their parents - former government agents - scramble to protect them from the intelligence agencies that once employed them.

seasons.review_body: Moving premiered on Disney+ Korea in August 2023 and became the platform's biggest Korean original by audience engagement metrics. Adapted from Kang Full's webtoon by director Park In-je, the 20-episode run makes an unusual structural choice: the first third belongs almost entirely to the parents. Ryu Seung-ryong, Han Hyo-joo, and Zo In-sung play former black-ops agents whose supernatural gifts - flight, regeneration, superhuman strength - were exploited by the state during the Cold War era. That generational weight gives the teenagers' story enormous emotional heft when it arrives. Critics at 100% on Rotten Tomatoes praised what multiple reviewers called the finest superhero storytelling in the Korean Wave: not spectacle-first, but character architecture that happens to have extraordinary action. Kate Sanchez of But Why Tho? noted it operates simultaneously as an action-heavyweight and narrative giant. The action sequences, particularly a mid-season highway chase and a late-season confrontation, set a new technical bar for Korean television. The 97% audience score reflects genuine cross-demographic passion.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere opens on the parents' generation - specifically on Ryu Seung-ryong's character before the teenagers are introduced - establishing that this is not a conventional superhero origin story. The Cold War spy framework arrives fully formed.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The opener's first display of a parent's power, which reframes what kind of show this will be.

critic_note.text: Moving is what you get when the world stops believing that super-powered beings in brightly coloured suits could actually save the day.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 9
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Widely cited as the series' single finest hour: a sustained action sequence set on a highway that critics and audiences identified as a landmark in Korean television craft. The episode works because the emotional stakes have been fully established by this point.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The highway sequence, which runs nearly uncut and plays at a scale that forced comparisons to theatrical action cinema.

critic_note.text: Moving isn't just a series that can be classified as an action-heavyweight. It's also a narrative giant as well.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 20
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale brings the generational reckoning to its conclusion, resolving the Cold War threads while leaving the next generation's story positioned for continuation. The emotional payoff for the parent arcs is the season's most affecting sequence.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final confrontation between a parent and the agency that shaped them, which pays off a full season of accumulated grief.
